sourceReviews.supportingSummary: Independently read the complete raw MCP JSON_MODIFY (Transact-SQL) article. Its newValue argument admits both nvarchar and numeric SQL types; the existing-path/non-NULL table row specifies replacement. Example C explicitly explains that a value not converted from text to a numeric SQL type is treated as text and enclosed in JSON string quotes. Existing numeric content does not make a new nvarchar argument numeric. The lax SQL NULL row supplies the separate deletion case. SQL Server 2016-and-later applicability covers SQL Server 2022, and the call uses JSON text rather than any native-json Preview extension.

choiceReviews.rationale: The actual @next declaration is nvarchar(10), with the nonnull text N'3'. The product contract uses the SQL argument type for JSON_MODIFY's new value; numeric-looking text is not automatically converted to a JSON number. Positive countercontext: with the shown valid text parameter, JSON_MODIFY(N'{"attempt":2}', '$.attempt', CAST(@next AS int)) would produce {"attempt":3} by supplying an int new value. That hypothetical numeric conversion is supported by the documented numeric-cast distinction but is absent from the frozen statement. It is not an executed result or an authored repair.

The existing $.attempt path is present, and the new argument is nonnull. The documented update row therefore replaces the old value; the original JSON number 2 is not retained by the shown invocation. Positive countercontext: JSON_MODIFY(N'{"attempt":2}', '$.attempt', 2) supplies a numeric SQL value equal to the original and has {"attempt":2} as the expected document. This is a successful numeric replacement with the same value, not evidence that the current update using N'3' is ignored.

Deletion in the default lax mode requires SQL NULL as the new value. The declared N'3' is nonnull text, so the existing attempt member is not deleted. Positive countercontext: JSON_MODIFY(N'{"attempt":2}', '$.attempt', NULL) uses the documented lax deletion rule and would yield {} because attempt is the sole member. This literal SQL NULL call supports the empty-object answer only under the changed new-value condition, not under the actual declaration.

The supplied @next remains nvarchar after assignment; its characters do not confer numeric SQL type. JSON_MODIFY updates the existing member with that text-typed value, so the documentation-derived result is {"attempt":"3"}. The original numeric 2 is replaced, not incremented or used to infer a target type. The product's explicit explanation about adding numeric casts is directly applicable to why D, rather than A, represents this unchanged expression.
